title: Rollback and Hotfix Orchestration Playbook + Status Messaging Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook describes a standardized, low-risk process for orchestrating rollbacks and emergency hotfixes when a production deployment causes customer impact or SLO degradation. It covers decision criteria, roles and responsibilities, step-by-step runbook actions for containment -> rollback -> hotfix -> verification, and ready-to-send status page & customer notification templates. Use this for incidents where a code/config change in Redwood services is the primary suspected cause.

Goals
- Restore customer-facing functionality within the contiguous SLO window (primary objective).
- Minimize blast radius and data loss.
- Execute predictable communication to customers and internal stakeholders.
- Produce clear handoff to Postmortem owners.

When to run this playbook (Triggers)
1) Error rate for an API route or model-serving path exceeds 5% for 5 minutes and sustained.
2) 99th percentile latency degrades >2x baseline for 10 minutes.
3) New deployment correlated with customer tickets or automated failure signals.
4) Feature flag rollback is possible and the change can be reverted within the minute.

Ownership and Roles
- Incident Lead (IL) — on-call SRE or service owner: coordinates decisions, authorizes rollback/hotfix.
- Deploy Executor (DE) — engineer with deploy permissions for the affected service.
- Communications Owner (CO) — customer success / incident comms lead: crafts status page and customer emails.
- QA Verifier (QV) — developer or QA assigned to smoke verification steps post-action.
- Postmortem Owner (PMO) — designated once service is stable (may be same as IL).

Escalation Matrix
- Tier 1 oncall (service): immediate contact via #oncall-alerts and phone + chat.
- Tier 2 SRE lead: if containment not achieved within 15 minutes.
- Engineering manager oncall: if rollback/hotfix has potential regulatory/customer data impact.

Quick reference table: SLO/thresholds and timeouts
| Item | Threshold | Action window |
|---|---:|---:|
| API 5xx rate | >5% sustained | Start playbook immediately (T0) |
| P99 latency | >2x baseline for 10min | Consider rollback if not explained by load |
| Error budget burn | >50% in 1hr | Notify platform leadership |
| Rollback safe? | Yes / No (see checklist) | Decide within 10 minutes |

Decision checklist: rollback vs. patch-in-place
- Is there a safe, tested rollback target within the last 24 hours? (Yes -> prefer rollback)
- Does the failure affect data integrity (writes) or only availability? (Data integrity -> avoid risky rollback)
- Is a feature flag available to toggle the behavior? (Feature-flag toggle quicker than code revert)
- Business impact: are key customers affected / SLO violations imminent? (High -> rollback to be conservative)

Runbook: Containment -> Rollback -> Hotfix -> Verify (step-by-step)
1) Initial triage (T0):
   - IL confirms signal source and alerts invited responders (add responders to incident bridge).
   - DE obtains deployment identifier (commit hash, image tag, release id) and notes the previous known-good target.
   - CO prepares a "we are investigating" status update template and posts to status page (see templates below).
2) Rapid containment (T0 + 0–10 minutes):
   - If feature flag present: toggle off flag to remove change. Document flag ID and time.
   - If routing change helps: shift traffic to an unaffected pool/region (use smart-routing runbook).
   - If neither possible and rollback candidate exists, prepare rollback.
3) Prepare rollback (T0 + 10 minutes):
   - DE validates the rollback artifact: checksum, deployment manifest, infra changes.
   - Run dry-run in staging that mirrors production config if available (5 min smoke).
   - Announce rollback intent to stakeholders: #incident, exec-notify if severity >= Sev2.
4) Execute rollback (T0 + 15–30 minutes):
   - Use the standardized deploy pipeline CLI:
     - kubectl rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> --namespace=prod --to-revision=<rev>
     - or deploy pipeline: redwood-deploy --service <svc> --image <previous-image> --reason "incident rollback"
   - DE monitors rollout health endpoints and metrics (error rate, p99, request per second).
   - If deployment orchestration fails, abort and escalate to SRE lead.
5) Post-rollback verification (T0 + 30–45 minutes):
   - QV executes core smoke tests (list below).
   - IL monitors for recurrence for 60 minutes.
   - CO updates status page: resolved or in recovery with ETA.
6) Hotfix path (if rollback not acceptable or rollback fails):
   - Branch and hotfix in a contained manner: create hotfix branch from last-good commit, apply minimal change with tests.
   - Run quick CI: unit + targeted integration tests (max 10–15 minutes).
   - Use canary rollout to 5% traffic; monitor for 10 minutes; expand if stable.
7) Post-incident wrap and handoff (once stable):
   - IL assigns PMO and opens postmortem ticket (link to template).
   - CO schedules customer follow-up if they received outage notices.

Smoke test checklist (run after rollback/hotfix)
- Auth login flow (token-based): success rate >= 99% for 50 synthetic requests.
- Core inference path: sample prompt latency <= baseline *1.5 and zero 500s for 5 minutes.
- Persistence sanity check: recent write-read consistency on a sample object.
- Health endpoints: /health and /metrics return 200 with expected metrics present.

Safety and governance rules
- No rollback modifying stateful migrations without manager approval.
- All production rollbacks must be recorded in the deployment audit log with reason and artifact IDs.
- If rollback affects billing or customer data retention, notify finance/legal immediately.

Status page and customer messaging templates
- Initial: Investigating
  Title: "We are investigating increased errors for <service>"
  Body: "We are currently investigating increased error rates and elevated latency affecting the <service> API. Our team has identified a recent deployment as a possible cause and is working on containment. We will post updates every 15 minutes or sooner when there is new information. Impact: some requests may return 5xx or be delayed. Affected regions: <regions>."

- Update: Action underway (example after rollback started)
  Title: "Action in progress: rolling back recent deployment for <service>"
  Body: "We are performing a rollback of a recent deployment to restore normal service. We expect recovery within 30 minutes. We are monitoring closely and will update as the rollback completes. If you are experiencing persistent errors after recovery, please contact support@redwood.ai with request IDs."

- Resolved: Recovery confirmed
  Title: "Recovered: <service> returned to normal operation"
  Body: "Service <service> has been restored to normal operation at <time> after a rollback/hotfix. Error rates and latency are within expected ranges. We will publish a post-incident report with root cause and remediation steps within 72 hours. Thank you for your patience."

- Customer-facing hotfix note (post-incident email template)
  Subject: "Service interruption for <service> on <date> — summary and next steps"
  Body: "Summary: At <start time> we observed increased errors for <service> caused by a deployment which we rolled back at <rollback time>. Impact: <describe customer-visible effects>. Current status: service restored. Postmortem: link to follow in 72 hours with action items. If you require immediate assistance, contact your CSM or support@redwood.ai."

Operational checklists and blocking conditions
- Do not rollback if: long-running migrations or irreversible schema changes are part of the target release unless database restore plan is pre-approved.
- Do not rollback if the incident is caused by upstream dependency (e.g., cloud provider outage); instead use traffic routing / fallback models.

Game day / exercise plan for this playbook
- Objective: validate rollback pipeline, communications cadence, and verification checks within a 1-hour window.
- Participants: oncall SRE, service owner, deploy executor, communications owner, QA verifier.
- Steps:
  1) Simulate a deployment that increases 5xx in blue environment.
  2) Trigger the playbook and time each phase.
  3) Evaluate status page timing and communication clarity.
  4) Post-exercise review: list 3 improvements and assign owners.

Evidence and logging requirements (what to attach to the postmortem)
- Deploy artifact IDs and rollout logs.
- Timestamps of feature flag toggles, traffic routing changes, and rollback execution with user IDs initiating actions.
- Metric graphs for error rate, latency, and traffic per region for the incident window.
- Customer tickets and support references affected during the incident.

Postmortem template (required fields)
- Title and incident ID
- Timeline with timestamps (UTC) for key events
- Root cause hypothesis and supporting evidence
- Actions taken (containment, rollback/hotfix) and why chosen
- Impact summary (SLOs breached, customers affected)
- Action items with owners and ETA for remediation

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Rollback checklist link: /confluence/eng-deploy/rollback-checklist
- Deploy pipeline: redwood-deploy (internal CLI) docs link: /confluence/eng-infra/deploy-pipeline
- Example deploy rollback command:
  redwood-deploy --service inference-api --image registry.redwood.ai/inference-api:2025-03-14-abcdef --reason "rollback due to 5xx spike"
- Healthcheck curl:
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://inference-api.redwood.ai/health || echo "health fail"

Last reviewed and notes
- This playbook was trialed in an internal game day on 2024-09-16 (see exercise notes) and updated for feature-flag-first approach on 2024-11-02.
- For questions or additions to the templates, contact the playbook owner: aisha.patel@redwood.ai.
